---
title: "Does the reconstruction hold against both reference photographs?"
subtitle: "Entry 01 fitted both store photographs and showed only the belly view. The studio frame is the one that catches what the belly hides, and nobody has seen it checked."
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| echo: false
ENTRY_CEILING = 180.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 500.0      # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 233.9     # s the probe actually used

import re

# Fit camera poses against both reference photographs
rgb_s, note_s = compare_to_photo(airplane, "studio", pose=(20.0, 209.6, -13.5))
rgb_b, note_b = compare_to_photo(airplane, "belly", pose=(36.0, 118.2, 19.7))

# Parse the camera and the residual out of each note. NO FALLBACKS: the
# first version of this cell defaulted every value when its regex missed,
# and when the note's format changed the page went on rendering the frozen
# literals as though they were live.
def _cam(note):
    m = re.search(r"camera\s*([\d\.]+)°\s*(ABOVE|BELOW),\s*"
                  r"azim\s*([\d\.-]+)°,\s*roll\s*([\d\.-]+)°", note)
    e = float(m.group(1))
    return (e if m.group(2) == "ABOVE" else -e,
            float(m.group(3)), float(m.group(4)))

def _resid(note):
    return float(re.search(r"Fit:\s*([\d\.]+)%\s*of\s*sqrt\(mask area\)",
                           note).group(1))

elev_s, azim_s, roll_s = _cam(note_s)
elev_b, azim_b, roll_b = _cam(note_b)
resid_s_pct = _resid(note_s)
resid_b_pct = _resid(note_b)
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{resid_s_pct:.2f}%"`]{.hero-value}
[studio outline chamfer residual relative to mask scale, confirming upper airframe geometry]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Yes, and the second view corrects the first. Both store photographs are taken from ABOVE — the fits return [`{python} f"{elev_s:.0f}"`°]{.key} and [`{python} f"{elev_b:.0f}"`°]{.key} of elevation — so the [initial reconstruction](2026-10-07-01-can-we-reconstruct-the-ft-f-16-viper-within-tolerance.qmd) was never checked against an underside at all, and this entry originally said otherwise because the reference photograph was labelled and described as a belly view when it is not. What the second frame adds is a second azimuth, not a second hemisphere: the bubble canopy, dorsal spine, leading-edge strakes and wingtip rails are seen twice from different bearings, and the fuselage underside and ventral fin remain unverified by any photograph (@fig-overlays).

The studio pose sits at azimuth [`{python} f"{azim_s:.0f}"`°]{.key} and roll [`{python} f"{roll_s:.1f}"`°]{.key}, for an outline residual of [`{python} f"{resid_s_pct:.2f}"`%]{.key} of mask scale. The in-flight frame sits at azimuth [`{python} f"{azim_b:.0f}"`°]{.key} and returns [`{python} f"{resid_b_pct:.2f}"`%]{.key}. Both poses are good and neither is improved by a second seed, so what is left is the model's shape rather than the camera's — unmodelled wingtip ordnance, canopy frame thickness and intake ducting. No gross loft or planform error is hidden in either bearing.

```{python}
#| label: fig-overlays
#| fig-cap: "Fitted model outlines against the studio frame (@fig-overlays, left) and the in-flight frame (@fig-overlays, right). Both cameras sit above the aircraft; the residuals are 2.0% and 2.9% of mask scale, and both are hedged because what remains at that level is shape rather than pose."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, (ax_s, ax_b) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5.5), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.3, 1]})
ax_s.imshow(rgb_s)
ax_s.set_axis_off()
ax_s.set_title("Studio front three-quarter view", fontsize=11)

ax_b.imshow(rgb_b)
ax_b.set_axis_off()
ax_b.set_title("In-flight view, from above and behind", fontsize=11)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
